main_text.p: quit)est calor præter naturam e corde in o-mne corpus effusus. Igitur pestilentem febrem morbis totius substantiae perperam attribuit Fernelius. Præterea pestilentium morborum caufam in aerem inquinatum duntaxat refert Fernelius, tametsi plures aliæ sint caufæ. Oritur interdum a fame:um de vulgo recte dicitur ἐν λιμῷ λοιμῷ [?]. Nā per urgentem famem agrestibus herbis, radicibus, alijsque prauum fuccum gignentibus pauperes vesci cogitur, unde primùm na-scitur pestis, quemadmodum oftendit Galenus, libro de Bono & Malo fucco. Idem quoq; lib. primo, de Febrium differentiis, è cacochymia pestilentem febrem interdum oriri absq; ulla aëris labe, his verbis demostrat. Quotquot(inquit)vitiosis cibariis fa-mem solari coacti fuere, putridis eos, ac pe-stilentibus magnam partem interiisse. Quin-etiam pestem unguentis, pulueribusq;ac alijs modis arte Sathanæ universo generi humano hostis infestissimi excogitatis, atque à veneficis exhibitis in populum dif-feminari, propagariq;, hactenus satis norunt Allobroges. page.notes: The Greek phrase ἐν λιμῷ λοιμῷ is only partly legible on the scan and is marked [?]. The catchword "ternas" sits at the lower right below the last line. "Quin-etiam" is hyphenated at the line end, and "ex-" is hyphenated at the page end, so the next word continues on the following page. Spelling was normalised for u/v and i/j per the rules (e.g. vitiosis, vesci). The word "norunt" is read from a faint print and may be doubtful.
